description: Response of Florida Shelf Ecosystems to Climate Change: The FLaSH Project is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); St. Petersburg Coastal and Marine Science Center; University of South Florida College of Marine Science. The FLaSH Ecosystem Project built upon earlier efforts to conduct benthic habitat mapping in Florida by including consideration of climate change impacts, particularly ocean acidification, on living marine resources along the shelf. Coverage: Coast of Florida (2010). The toolkit gives Coast of Florida as the location, 2010 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

Scientists studied ocean chemistry to better understand the impacts of higher levels of atmospheric CO2 on marine and coastal resources, and created resources to inform potential remediation efforts...
